scholarships.title: Duke University Karsh International Scholars Program

existing.description: The Karsh International Scholarship was founded at Duke University in 2010 through a donation from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh. It brings together a cohort of international undergraduates who promote interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research and scholarship in the service of society. International applicants must have demonstrated financial need to be eligible. The award covers tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need beyond those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships and other career-advancing opportunities. There is no separate application: candidates apply to Duke University and request financial aid.
eligibility: Citizen of a country outside the United States
Does not already hold a B.A. or B.S. degree
Demonstrated financial need for financial aid
Must apply to Duke University; there is no separate application and nominations are not accepted
existing.eligibility_summary: International (non-U.S. citizen, non-dual-citizen) applicants who apply to Duke University and demonstrate documented financial need. Applicants who already hold a B.A. or B.S. are not eligible, and students cannot be nominated for the scholarship.
benefits: Tuition, room and board and mandatory fees
Membership in the Karsh International Scholars cohort with a faculty director
coverage: Funding for three summers for research, unpaid internships and career-advancing opportunities
requirements: Complete the Duke financial aid forms
application_method: Apply to Duke University via the standard undergraduate admission process
Request financial aid and complete the Duke financial aid forms
existing.selection_notes: Strong academic preparation and documented need for financial aid are the stated selection criteria; there is no separate scholarship application, essay or nomination route.
existing.best_fit: High-achieving international first-year applicants to Duke who can document significant financial need.
existing.notes: Endowed in 2010 by Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh. The current cohort spans Botswana, Bulgaria, Chile, Egypt, England, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Madagascar, Mongolia, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Pakistan, Russia, Rwanda, South Africa, Syria, Tajikistan, Thailand, Tunisia, Vietnam and Zimbabwe. Faculty Director: Dr. Giovanni Zanalda.
existing.application_period: Tied to Duke University's undergraduate admission cycle; the programme page publishes no separate window.
existing.deadline_display: No separate application or scholarship deadline is published. The official page states "Simply apply to Duke University" and directs applicants to the Duke Financial Aid website; consideration therefore follows Duke University's own admission cycle.
existing.program_type: Merit and need-based university scholarship for international undergraduates, awarded by Duke University's Office of University Scholars and Fellows
